parts.markdown:
Use our free **Nebraska paycheck calculator** to estimate your take-home pay after federal income tax, Nebraska income tax, Social Security, Medicare and other employee deductions.

Enter your annual salary or hourly earnings, select your payment frequency and customize your withholding information to see how much money you could receive on payday.

Nebraska's payroll withholding system includes state-specific allowance deductions, progressive percentage tables and special minimum withholding requirements for certain employers.

Whether you work in Omaha, Lincoln, Bellevue, Grand Island or another Nebraska community, understanding these deductions can help you compare salaries and manage monthly expenses.

## How to Use the Nebraska Paycheck Calculator

Choose annual salary if you receive fixed compensation or hourly wages if your earnings depend on working hours.

Enter your gross earnings before taxes and deductions.

Select your payment frequency. Enter the federal and Nebraska income tax withheld for the pay period from your pay stub.

Include retirement contributions, healthcare premiums and other employee deductions. Use the full withholding amounts, including any extra tax withheld.

Review your estimated paycheck breakdown to understand how much of your gross income remains after applicable deductions.

Use your latest payroll statement and withholding certificate for greater accuracy.

## How Nebraska Income Tax Withholding Works

Nebraska publishes Circular EN, which contains its official employer income tax withholding instructions.

The 2026 version applies to qualifying wages paid on or after January 1, 2026.

Employers calculate withholding using the applicable payroll-period wage bracket tables or percentage method.

The withholding calculation accounts for the appropriate allowance amount before applying the relevant percentage schedule.

Nebraska's payroll withholding rates and brackets should not automatically be replaced with the rates used to calculate an individual's final annual income tax return.

Read the official [2026 Nebraska Circular EN](https://revenue.nebraska.gov/sites/default/files/doc/business/Cir_En_2025/2026cir_en_whole.pdf) for the applicable calculation methodology.

## Understanding Nebraska Form W-4N

Nebraska employees generally provide state withholding information through Form W-4N.

The form records applicable withholding allowances and additional withholding information.

The 2026 annual withholding allowance value is $2,440 per applicable allowance.

Employees with older withholding certificates may require different treatment depending on the form version and applicable state instructions.

The modern federal Form W-4 does not use the same allowance structure.

Consequently, federal withholding information should not automatically be copied into Nebraska allowance fields.

Review your state certificate when your employment or household circumstances change.

## Nebraska's Special Minimum Withholding Requirement

Nebraska has a special income tax withholding rule that can affect employees working for larger employers.

Employers with more than 24 employees generally must withhold at least 1.5% of an employee's taxable wages.

A lower amount may be withheld if the employee provides appropriate documentation supporting the lower withholding amount.

Relevant documentation can include information about qualifying dependents, marital status or itemized deductions.

For example, if an employee has $1,000 in taxable wages and the special requirement applies, the ordinary minimum withholding amount is:

$1,000 × 1.5% = $15

If the standard withholding calculation produces only $8 and no qualifying documentation supports lower withholding, the applicable minimum would affect the final deduction.

This is why employer circumstances matter when calculating Nebraska take-home pay.

## Nebraska Withholding Calculation Example

Suppose an employee has $1,000 in adjusted weekly wages after the applicable withholding allowance has already been subtracted.

The applicable weekly single withholding bracket begins at $772.

Using the published base tax of $25.85 and marginal withholding rate of 4.48%:

$25.85 + (($1,000 − $772) × 0.0448)

The ordinary withholding estimate is approximately $36.06.

Any applicable special minimum withholding requirement or additional withholding request must also be considered.

This example uses adjusted wages rather than the employee's original gross paycheck.

## Federal Taxes Deducted From Nebraska Paychecks

Nebraska employees remain subject to applicable federal income tax withholding.

Federal withholding depends on taxable earnings, filing status, payroll frequency and Form W-4 information.

Social Security generally applies at 6.2% of covered earnings up to the 2026 annual taxable wage ceiling of $184,500.

Ordinary Medicare withholding applies at 1.45% of covered wages.

Employers generally withhold an additional 0.9% when Medicare-covered wages paid by that employer exceed $200,000 during the calendar year.

Consult [IRS Publication 15-T](https://www.irs.gov/publications/p15t) and the [IRS Employer's Tax Guide](https://www.irs.gov/publications/p15) for official federal payroll calculation procedures.

## Nebraska Hourly Paycheck Calculator

Hourly employees can estimate gross earnings by multiplying their hourly wage by regular working hours and adding qualifying overtime compensation.

Suppose an employee earns $25 per hour and works 40 regular hours plus seven overtime hours at time-and-a-half.

Regular earnings:

$25 × 40 = $1,000

Overtime earnings:

$25 × 1.5 × 7 = $262.50

Total gross earnings:

$1,262.50

Applicable taxes and deductions are then calculated using their respective taxable wage amounts.

Employees receiving shift differentials, commissions or bonuses may experience different withholding amounts.

Review the [US Department of Labor overtime requirements](https://www.dol.gov/agencies/whd/overtime) for additional guidance.

## Does Nebraska Have Local Income Taxes?

Nebraska municipalities generally do not impose separate personal wage income taxes on ordinary employee compensation.

Employees working in Omaha or Lincoln therefore generally do not encounter additional municipal wage taxes of the kind found in certain cities in Missouri, Ohio or Michigan.

However, local taxes on purchases and household expenses can still influence disposable income.

Evaluate these expenses separately when comparing employment opportunities.

## Working Across Nebraska State Borders

Nebraska workers may live in Iowa, South Dakota, Kansas or another neighboring state while working in Nebraska.

A residence in a state without individual wage income tax does not automatically eliminate Nebraska income tax on qualifying Nebraska-sourced earnings.

Remote work and short-term employment assignments may also involve special income sourcing rules.

Nebraska has specific provisions affecting nonresident employees attending qualifying training or conferences and other multi-state employment arrangements.

Consult the official Circular EN guidance before applying a nonresident withholding exemption.

## Planning Your Nebraska Monthly Budget

Build your [household budget](/calculators/budget-calculator/) using estimated take-home pay rather than gross salary.

Include housing, transportation, groceries, utilities, healthcare and required debt payments.

When comparing employment offers, consider insurance premiums, employer retirement matching and paid leave alongside your estimated net income.

Our [emergency fund calculator](/savings/emergency-fund-calculator/) can help establish a suitable savings target, while our [debt-to-income ratio calculator](/debt/debt-to-income-ratio-calculator/) can help evaluate existing borrowing obligations.

## Frequently Asked Questions

### Does Nebraska have a minimum paycheck withholding requirement?

Employers with more than 24 employees generally must withhold at least 1.5% of taxable wages unless appropriate documentation supports lower withholding.

### What is Nebraska's withholding allowance in 2026?

The annual withholding allowance value is $2,440 per applicable allowance. Employees should follow their Form W-4N information and the official withholding instructions.

### Does Omaha have a separate personal wage income tax?

Omaha generally does not impose a separate personal wage income tax. Applicable federal and Nebraska state taxes still reduce employee earnings.
